topStories.headline: Chinatown's $150 Million Transformation Reaches Peak Disruption — Broadway Tunnel Closes Sunday
topStories.dek: A full closure of the Broadway Tunnel begins Sunday as San Francisco undertakes its largest investment in Chinatown infrastructure in decades.
topStories.body:
San Francisco's Chinatown is in the thick of a multi-front construction surge this week as three simultaneous public works projects reshape the neighborhood's key corridors. The Broadway Tunnel is scheduled to be fully closed from 7 a.m. Sunday, August 16, through 5 a.m. Monday, August 17, followed immediately by a partial closure — one bore at a time — lasting through approximately October 2027. The closures are tied to seismic retrofitting and other upgrades at the Chinatown Public Health Center, which sits directly atop the tunnel's east entrance.

Separately, the pedestrian bridge connecting Portsmouth Square to the Hilton Hotel on Kearny Street has been demolished as part of the $73 million Portsmouth Square Improvement Project. According to the San Francisco Recreation and Park Department, crews completed removal of the bridge section over Kearny during the first of two full weekend closures in early August, with partial lane restrictions on Kearny Street between Clay and Washington continuing through August 15. The Portsmouth Square garage will reopen to normal operations as the partial closures wind down.

City officials say removing the 300-foot concrete-and-steel bridge will unlock 20,000 additional square feet of usable open space, setting the stage for a redesigned plaza with a flexible outdoor event stage, a new zero-carbon community clubhouse, and improved sight lines throughout the square. Construction is expected to wrap by mid-2028. A third project — renovation of the Chinatown branch library — rounds out the trifecta at a combined cost of $150 million across all three efforts.

Drivers and Muni riders are advised to allow extra travel time and check SFMTA.com/GoChinatown for the latest detour maps and transit reroutes before heading into the neighborhood. The 8 Bayshore bus will continue operating with adjusted stops during various closure phases.

topStories.headline: The Huntington Hotel Is Back: Nob Hill's Storied Grande Dame Reopened This Spring
topStories.dek: After five years shuttered and a sweeping renovation, the Huntington Hotel on Nob Hill reopened in March 2026 with reimagined interiors, a revitalized spa, and the return of the beloved Big Four restaurant.
topStories.body:
One of Nob Hill's most iconic addresses is welcoming guests again. The Huntington Hotel, at 1075 California Street, reopened on March 2, 2026, following a comprehensive restoration led by Flynn Properties and Highgate after the hotel closed during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. The 12-story Georgian-style brick building — added to the National Register of Historic Places in September 2025 — now offers 71 guest rooms and 72 suites, with interior design by San Francisco's own Ken Fulk that honors the building's 1920s architectural bones while introducing modern comforts.

The revived hotel brings back two beloved institutions under one roof: the Nob Hill Spa, reimagined as a three-level wellness destination, and the Big Four restaurant, which reopened in its 50th anniversary year alongside a new bar called Arabella's. The restaurant, named for the railroad tycoons who once dominated the hilltop, features a revamped menu and updated dining space while retaining its storied atmosphere.

The Huntington has long attracted luminaries including Truman Capote, Marlene Dietrich, and Princess Margaret. Its return signals growing confidence in Nob Hill's hospitality sector, alongside the ongoing centennial celebrations at the InterContinental Mark Hopkins next door. The hotel's intimate scale — averaging around 581 square feet per room, nearly three times the industry standard — underscores its positioning as an urban retreat rather than a convention property.

topStories.headline: Top of the Mark Toasts 100 Years With a 100-Martini Revival
topStories.dek: The InterContinental Mark Hopkins San Francisco is celebrating its centennial year with year-round special events, including the return of the legendary 100 Martini Passport program at its iconic sky lounge.
topStories.body:
The InterContinental Mark Hopkins San Francisco, perched atop Nob Hill at 999 California Street, is marking a milestone in 2026: the hotel's 100th anniversary, with the official centennial date falling on December 4. To anchor a year of celebrations, the hotel revived its famed 100 Martini experience at Top of the Mark on May 25, 2026. Guests receive a passport-styled booklet and earn a stamp with each martini ordered from a menu of 100 drinks ranging from classic preparations to contemporary spirit-forward cocktails, priced between $22 and $26.

Throughout the centennial year, the hotel is rolling out curated guest experiences, historical storytelling, culinary programming, and special events tracing the property's century atop one of the city's most recognizable hills. The Top of the Mark, a 19th-floor sky lounge with nearly 360-degree views of the bay and skyline, has been a gathering place for San Franciscans since its original opening in 1939 — including serving as a farewell stop for tens of thousands of World War II servicemen.

The hotel is also hosting monthly dance evenings in the Peacock Court ballroom, led by bandleader Alex Mendham and his 11-piece orchestra, as part of the centennial series. Guests and locals interested in sharing memories of the Mark Hopkins are invited to do so at TheCentennialMark@ihg.com.

moreNews.headline: Sam Wo Chinatown Restaurant Thriving Under New Ownership After September 2025 Reopening
moreNews.body: After the closure of the century-old Sam Wo restaurant in January 2025 when longtime owner David Ho retired, the Chinatown institution at 713 Clay Street reopened in September 2025 under new ownership led by Bay Area restaurateurs Norris Song and Ming Duong. The revived restaurant has maintained most of the beloved original menu, including its signature BBQ pork rice noodle rolls, fish porridge, and dim sum staples, while honoring the restaurant's more-than-100-year heritage in San Francisco's Chinatown.

moreNews.headline: FITNESS SF Coming to Polk Gulch: 42,000-Sq-Ft Gym Slated for September Opening
moreNews.body: A major new fitness facility is on the way for Polk Gulch, Russian Hill, and Nob Hill residents. FITNESS SF Polk is scheduled to open in September 2026 at 1600 Jackson Street in a 42,000-square-foot space at the heart of the Polk corridor. The gym — a new location from the local FITNESS SF chain — was developed with extensive community input, including survey feedback and behind-the-scenes tours for neighbors. Founding memberships are currently available at pre-sale pricing through the company's website before the grand opening.

moreNews.headline: Kearny Street Partial Closures Continue Through August 15 as Bridge Demolition Wraps
moreNews.body: San Francisco Recreation and Parks confirmed this week that demolition of the Kearny Street pedestrian bridge at Portsmouth Square is on schedule and nearly complete. During the first of two full-weekend closures in early August, crews successfully removed the section of the bridge spanning over Kearny Street. Partial closures on Kearny between Clay and Washington streets continue through August 15, with at least two lanes remaining open at all times. The Portsmouth Square garage remains open during partial closure periods; local business access on the east side of Kearny is maintained throughout.

restaurants.name: Sushi Sato

restaurants.name: Bar Bibi
restaurants.description: A Nob Hill natural wine bar with excellent small plates, also home to Better Half Coffee during daytime hours.

restaurants.name: Top of the Mark

restaurants.name: Café Nook

restaurants.name: Great Eastern Restaurant

restaurants.name: House of Nanking

restaurants.name: Ramen Sho Ryu
restaurants.description: A quick and satisfying ramen shop in Nob Hill, popular for its rich broths and convenient location for a fast weeknight dinner.

shops.name: Best Cleaners

shops.name: Polanco
shops.type: Mexican folk art and fine art gallery shop
shops.description: A Polk Street shop and gallery specializing in authentic Mexican folk art, fine crafts, and Day of the Dead collectibles.

shops.name: Cottage Industry
shops.description: A charming Polk Gulch shop carrying a curated selection of home décor, gifts, cards, and locally made goods.

shops.name: The Wok Shop

shops.description: A unique Chinatown shop specializing in Chinese musical instruments — erhu, guzheng, pipa — alongside world music instruments and sheet music.

artEntertainment.type: Gothic Episcopal cathedral and cultural venue

artEntertainment.name: The Masonic
artEntertainment.description: A 3,300-seat Nob Hill concert hall and event venue hosting major national and international touring acts in an intimate setting.

artEntertainment.description: A Chinatown cultural hub offering art exhibitions, community programs, history tours, and educational resources celebrating Chinese and Chinese American heritage.

gymsRecreation.name: Mighty Pilates Russian Hill
gymsRecreation.description: A Polk Gulch–area Pilates studio offering reformer, functional, and fit Pilates classes for all levels.

gymsRecreation.description: The revived Nob Hill Spa inside the freshly reopened Huntington Hotel, reimagined as a three-level wellness destination with a pool, fitness center, and treatment rooms.

gymsRecreation.name: St. Mary's Square
